messages:
alex: Heads-up — I started a pass on the docs glossary/terminology. Found ~25 ambiguous entries (model/model family/model variant, hosted vs dedicated, runtime vs serving). Proposing we: map each term to an owner, define the canonical phrasing, and add a single example usage. Prefer lots of small PRs (<10 files) over one big sweep.

maria: +1. Strong ask: add a rule for 'model' vs 'model family' vs 'model variant' — it's leaking into SDK snippets and confuses users. Also we should standardize whether we use 'model_id' or 'model' in examples.

shreyas: Agree. For SDK examples let's standardize parameter names to match the SDK surface (e.g., model_id in Python, model in JS if that's how the SDK exposes it). Also add a short "migration note" template for breaking renames.

june: For product names, I recommend Title Case (Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private). For feature-level terms use sentence case (serving runtime, token caching). Also, we should prefer 'Dedicated capacity' over 'Dedicated' in text to avoid ambiguity.

docs-bot: Created tracker issue #1423 with proposed owner map and the initial term list. Link: https://github.internal/redwood/docs/ISSUE-1423 (will populate owners as people volunteer).

alex: Process proposal: 1) Pick a handful of related terms (2-6), 2) open a small PR with the glossary row + 1 example + any inline snippet changes, 3) request approval from the term owner + one engineering review. Add a tiny automated check: run a search to show files touched by the term so reviewers can eyeball collateral. Example command I ran:

```bash
rg "\b(Redwood Dedicated|redwood-dedicated)\b" docs/ -n || true
```

This prints occurrences; include the output as a file in the PR.

maria: I'll take Python SDK snippets and the 'model naming' cluster. @shreyas can you own JS snippets?

shreyas: Yup I'll take JS. I'll also add a small doctest-like harness to validate the Python snippets at CI time (cover basic imports and param names).

june: We need to ensure old links keep working. If we change glossary slugs, we should add redirects. I'll coordinate with eng-infra for a redirect PR (probably under docs-redirects repo).

alex: Timeline: owners assigned in the tracker by EOD Friday, first small PRs next week, rollout over 2 weeks. If anyone objects to specific canonical terms (e.g., 'inference runtime' vs 'serving runtime') speak up now.

maria: I prefer 'serving runtime' in top-level product pages and 'inference runtime' in infra deep dives — keeps consumer docs simpler.

shreyas: :+1: for that split.

alex: OK — I'll draft a 1-page style guidance (voice + a small table of canonical terms + examples) and paste it into the tracker. Will tag owners and link to PR template for glossary changes.

june: Also: add a checklist item for redirects and for updating SDK release notes if naming affects public APIs.

alex: Perfect. Thanks all — small PRs, owner approvals, snippet CI checks. cc @docs-bot to keep the tracker updated.

docs-bot: Noted — I'll post updates to the tracker when PRs are opened and ping reviewers. :robot_face:

maria: Thanks — excited to get the sheets cleaned up.

shreyas: I'll start a draft PR for JS snippets this afternoon.

alex: Awesome — keep things bite-sized and leave notes in the PR about why phrasing was chosen (one-liner rationale).
